title: Model deprecation transition playbook and enterprise readiness checklist
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create a practical playbook and checklist for handling third-party model deprecations/major version changes that could affect enterprise customers. Deliverables include a detection & alerting matrix, compatibility test suite requirements, migration communication templates, a staged rollout plan (canary / phased), pricing and SLA impact guidelines, and a decision rubric for automatic fallback vs. forced migration. This is driven by recent vendor churn and customer questions about model stability and predictable behaviour.
tasks: Inventory current externally-hosted and supported model variants and map customers to active model pins
Define signal types for deprecation: vendor EOL notices, repository forks, critical CVEs, accuracy regressions from eval harness
Specify a minimal compatibility test suite (prompt set, tokenization checks, deterministic outputs where required)
Draft customer communication templates (Advance Notice, Technical Migration Notes, Post-Migration Validation)
Design rollback and fallback policies (automatic routing to pinned variant, suggest equivalent model families)
Estimate cost and latency delta matrix for suggested migration options (quantized vs. full-precision, batch sizes)
Coordinate legal/contract review for SLA changes and notify Sales/CS playbooks
acceptance_criteria: Playbook doc reviewed and approved by PM, two Engineering leads, and Solutions Eng
Compatibility test suite defined with pass/fail criteria and a CI integration ticket created
Two customer-facing templates approved by Legal and Customer Success
Migration runbook validated in lab with one non-critical internal customer and results captured
Dashboard alerts wired for vendor deprecation signals (RSS / vendor API / GH release tags)

risks: High-volume customers pinned to deprecated model variants may face functional regressions if migrations are rushed
Complex tokenization differences across forks could require bespoke migration engineering per customer
Automatic fallback could mask regressions while increasing cost due to inefficient model selection
Legal/Sales pushback on SLA adjustments may delay customer notifications
outcomes: A templated, repeatable process for detecting and executing model transitions with minimal customer disruption
CI-backed compatibility checks that catch regressions before customer exposure
Clear go/no-go criteria for automated versus manual migrations
Customer communication bundles and CS playbooks that reduce support load during migrations
observations: Competitors are accelerating model churn by pushing major model updates without enterprise transition tooling
Some large customers prefer vendor-locked stable variants, creating an opportunity for Redwood to differentiate with a robust transition story
Market interest in SLA visibility for model stability is increasing among regulated verticals
market_signals: Multiple RFPs citing 'model stability' as a mandatory requirement in the last quarter
